dialect.guess: IBM Enterprise COBOL or Micro Focus COBOL (JMA ORCA project, likely compiled with OpenCOBOL/GnuCOBOL on Linux)
evidence: LINKAGE SECTION with USING clause on PROCEDURE DIVISION

purpose.summary: This is a dispatcher/controller program for a patient-count aggregation report in the JMA ORCA medical receipt software system. It parses command-line parameters, then routes execution to one of several sub-programs (A00000C110 through A00000C120) based on report type (by department, doctor, age, region, insurance) and inpatient/outpatient flag. It is part of the 'daily ledger' subsystem.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese medical receipt processing)

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY statements for modular include files (CPCOMMONSHELL.INC, CPERRFL.INC, CPORCSPRTLNK.INC, etc.)
EVALUATE used as a dispatch table to call 11 different sub-programs
UNSTRING used to parse comma-delimited command-line parameters
Japanese comments encoded in EUC-JP or Shift-JIS (rendered as latin-1 mojibake)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — DB access delegated to called sub-programs
LINKAGE SECTION with COMMAND-PARAM PIC X(256) for shell invocation
JMA Open Source License header (ORCA project)
verdict.notes: The file is decoded as latin-1 but the comments contain Japanese text originally encoded in EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, appearing as mojibake. The program is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system used in Japanese clinics. All four COBOL divisions are present and the structure is consistent with production-grade batch COBOL. The tab character visible in the WRK-POSTMAEG area is a minor anomaly in an otherwise fixed-format file.
